text:
maria: Heads-up — we're updating the JS/TS SDK and need a final decision on the HTTP client story (undici vs global fetch). This affects ESM/CJS packaging, edge runtime compatibility, and TS types. Thoughts?

adrian: High level: prefer accepting a user-supplied fetch and defaulting to the best runtime option. Avoid forcing undici on edge runtimes.

maria: Agreed. But we need concrete behavior for three targets: Node (server), edge runtimes (Vercel/Cloudflare/Workers/Deno), and bundlers (next/x).

jess: Practical approach I've used: SDK checks for global fetch first, then tries dynamic import of 'undici' in Node if no global. Something like:
```js
const DEFAULT_FETCH = globalThis.fetch || (await import('undici')).fetch;
```
That keeps edges untouched.

adrian: That works but watch ESM/CJS import semantics. dynamic import('undici') only works in ESM contexts or with Babel/packagers that handle it. For CJS consumers we should avoid top-level static imports of undici.

kevin: For TypeScript typing: if we call userFetch(fetch) we should export a Fetch type alias so callers with lib:dom or "dom-fetch" types align. E.g.:
```ts
export type FetchFn = typeof fetch;
export function createClient(opts: { fetch?: FetchFn }) { ... }
```
That way people with differing lib settings can pass their fetch and TS stays happy.

maria: Good point. Also we have customers on Node 16-ish using SDK via CJS. How do we avoid runtime crashes if undici isn't installed?

jess: Make undici an optional peer dependency or a regular dependency but lazy-load it and catch import errors. If import fails, surface clear error: "No fetch available: install undici or pass a fetch implementation". Don't throw at import time.

adrian: Packaging note: use conditional exports in package.json so ESM consumers get ESM bundle and CJS get CJS. But the runtime fetch resolution should be inside the runtime entry, not in build-time require(). Example package.json snippet:
```json
{"exports": { 
  ".": {
    "import": "./dist/esm/index.js",
    "require": "./dist/cjs/index.js"
  }
}}
```

kevin: Edge runtimes: never import undici there. Workers/Deno/Bun have their own fetch implementations and you can't polyfill them reliably. For Cloudflare Workers, just rely on global fetch. For Deno, recommend passing globalThis.fetch. For Bun, same.

maria: What about bundlers? Next.js + Webpack sometimes polyfills node built-ins, which can be weird if we ship code that imports 'undici'.

adrian: Two mitigations: 1) lazy/dynamic import only when needed (server-only code path), 2) provide a tiny ESM shim that only references fetch detection logic and doesn't import undici in the browser bundle. Also mark undici as optional to keep client bundles small.

jess: We should update sample apps and quickstarts demonstrating: (a) server-side Node example using undici fallback, (b) edge example showing passing global fetch, (c) how to configure in next.js getServerSideProps or app router. Keep code snippets copy-paste ready.

maria: I can write the three short samples. Any preference for the SDK API surface? Right now we have new Client({ apiKey }) — should we add Client({ fetch, ... }) param?

kevin: Yes do that. Also support client.fetch = customFetch for later runtime change. And document type: "If you don't pass a fetch, SDK will use globalThis.fetch when available, otherwise try optional undici on Node. If neither available, throws with an actionable message."

adrian: CI and tests: add matrix for Node 16/18/20, Cloudflare Worker (minitest), and Deno (basic). Also test that importing the SDK in browser-like bundlers doesn't pull undici into bundle (use webpack/bun analyzer).

maria: Sounds good. One more: telemetry and retries rely on Headers init — undici's fetch has subtle differences (Headers class). We should normalize at the boundary: map Headers to our internal header abstraction to avoid surprises.

jess: Yup, and document that AbortSignal compatibility is required for retries/timeouts. If a runtime's fetch doesn't support AbortSignal properly, users should pass a polyfilled fetch.

maria: I'll draft changes: PR will add optional fetch param, lazy-undici loader, TS FetchFn export, samples, and docs. ETA EOD Friday. Anyone wants to pair on the implementation?

adrian: I can review the loader logic and packaging changes.

kevin: I'll add TS tests and update samples.

sdk-bot: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/432 — draft - WIP

maria: Thanks all — linking draft RFC after PR lands for final signoff. :sparkles:
